submission.justification: Absorber-F2 with 5mm plate thickness achieves the best energy resolution of 3.223% at 100 GeV among all tested configurations. This represents approximately 15% better resolution than the best Absorber-F1 configuration (3.819% at 4mm) and 35% better than the best Absorber-F3 configuration (4.947% at 6mm). The simulation sweep across thicknesses from 2-8mm shows that F2 performs optimally at 5mm, with performance degrading at both thinner and thicker plates. All three candidate materials are compatible with the mechanical support design and can be machined to required tolerances. No explicit constraints regarding activation or hands-on maintenance were documented that would exclude any of the candidates, suggesting all three materials are viable from a radiation safety perspective. The 5mm thickness falls well within the specified 2-10mm constraint range.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 at 5mm achieves 3.223% energy resolution, which is the best among all tested configurations across all three materials and thickness ranges.

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 is one of the three candidate materials listed: Absorber-F1, Absorber-F2, and Absorber-F3.

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: All three candidate materials are documented as compatible with the mechanical support design. No explicit activation or radiation safety concerns were documented that would prevent hands-on maintenance for any candidate, including Absorber-F2.
The recommended plate thickness of 5mm falls within the specified range of 2-10mm.
